original: When addSink is called with a no-op sink, then it returns a function.
refined: After calling addSink(() => {}), the returned value is a function

original: When a sink is registered and logger.info is called with stage "verify" and message "no test command", then the sink receives an entry whose message equals "no test command".
refined: After addSink(fn), calling logger.info({ stage: 'verify', message: 'no test command' }) invokes fn once with object.message === 'no test command'

original: When a sink is registered and a log call uses stage "verify", then the received entry has stage "verify".
refined: After addSink(fn), calling logger.info({ stage: 'verify', message: 'test' }) invokes fn with object.stage === 'verify'

original: When a sink is registered and logger.warn is called, then the received entry has level "warn".
refined: After addSink(fn), calling logger.warn('test') invokes fn with object.level === 'warn'

original: When a sink receives an entry, then its timestamp parses as an ISO-8601 date.
refined: After addSink(fn), any log call invokes fn where new Date(object.timestamp).toISOString().startsWith(new Date().getFullYear().toString()) is true (valid ISO-8601)

original: When a story-scoped logger emits an entry, then the sink receives the supplied story identifier in storyId.
refined: After addSink(fn), calling logger.info({ storyId: 'story-abc' }) invokes fn with object.storyId === 'story-abc'

original: When logging data with apiKey "sk-live-abc123", then the sink receives data.apiKey equal to "[REDACTED]".
refined: After addSink(fn), calling logger.info({ data: { apiKey: 'sk-live-abc123' } }) invokes fn with object.data.apiKey === '[REDACTED]'

original: When logging message "token ghp_0123456789abcdefghij failed", then the sink receives message "token [REDACTED] failed".
refined: After addSink(fn), calling logger.info('token ghp_0123456789abcdefghij failed') invokes fn with object.message === 'token [REDACTED] failed'

original: When the unsubscribe function returned by addSink is invoked, then that sink receives no subsequent log entries.
refined: const unsub = addSink(fn); unsub(); logger.info('test'); fn is never called

original: When two sinks are registered and one log call occurs, then both sinks receive the entry.
refined: After addSink(fn1) and addSink(fn2), calling logger.info('test') invokes fn1 and fn2 each exactly once with the same entry

original: When the first registered sink throws during a log call, then a later registered sink still receives the entry.
refined: After addSink(() => { throw new Error('sink error') }) and addSink(fn2), calling logger.info('test') invokes fn2 with entry.message === 'test' and does not throw

original: When a registered sink throws and a file path is configured, then the JSONL file still receives the entry.
refined: With logger configured with filePath and addSink(() => { throw new Error() }), after logger.info('test') the JSONL file contains an entry with message 'test'

original: When a registered sink throws, then the originating log call does not throw.
refined: After addSink(() => { throw new Error('sink error') }), calling logger.info('test') completes without throwing

original: When buildResourceAttributes is called with a service name, then it returns service.name equal to that service name.
refined: Call buildResourceAttributes({ serviceName: 'my-service', runId: '123' }) and assert the returned array contains exactly one entry with key='service.name' and value='my-service'.

original: When buildResourceAttributes is called with a run identifier, then it returns nax.run_id equal to that identifier.
refined: Call buildResourceAttributes({ serviceName: 'svc', runId: 'run-456' }) and assert the returned array contains exactly one entry with key='nax.run_id' and value='run-456'.

original: When buildResourceAttributes is called with a feature name, then it returns nax.feature equal to that name.
refined: Call buildResourceAttributes({ serviceName: 'svc', runId: '123', feature: 'my-feature' }) and assert the returned array contains exactly one entry with key='nax.feature' and value='my-feature'.

original: When buildResourceAttributes is called with a project name, then it returns nax.project equal to that name.
refined: Call buildResourceAttributes({ serviceName: 'svc', runId: '123', project: 'my-project' }) and assert the returned array contains exactly one entry with key='nax.project' and value='my-project'.

original: When buildResourceAttributes is called, then it returns nax.version equal to NAX_VERSION.
refined: Call buildResourceAttributes({ serviceName: 'svc', runId: '123' }) and assert the returned array contains exactly one entry with key='nax.version' and value equal to process.env.NAX_VERSION.

original: When buildResourceAttributes is called, then it returns host.name equal to the operating system hostname.
refined: Call buildResourceAttributes({ serviceName: 'svc', runId: '123' }) and assert the returned array contains exactly one entry with key='host.name' and value equal to os.hostname().

original: When buildResourceAttributes is called, then it returns process.pid as a numeric attribute equal to the current process identifier.
refined: Call buildResourceAttributes({ serviceName: 'svc', runId: '123' }) and assert the returned array contains exactly one entry with key='process.pid' where typeof value === 'number' and value === process.pid.

original: When buildResourceAttributes is called with a branch name, then it returns nax.git.branch equal to that branch.
refined: Call buildResourceAttributes({ serviceName: 'svc', runId: '123', git: { branch: 'main' } }) and assert the returned array contains exactly one entry with key='nax.git.branch' and value='main'.

original: When buildResourceAttributes is called with a commit sha, then it returns nax.git.sha equal to that sha.
refined: Call buildResourceAttributes({ serviceName: 'svc', runId: '123', git: { sha: 'abc123' } }) and assert the returned array contains exactly one entry with key='nax.git.sha' and value='abc123'.

original: When no branch is supplied, then the returned attributes contain no nax.git.branch key.
refined: Call buildResourceAttributes({ serviceName: 'svc', runId: '123' }) (without git.branch) and assert no entry in the returned array has key='nax.git.branch'.

original: When no commit sha is supplied, then the returned attributes contain no nax.git.sha key.
refined: Call buildResourceAttributes({ serviceName: 'svc', runId: '123' }) (without git.sha) and assert no entry in the returned array has key='nax.git.sha'.

original: When buildTracesPayload creates a payload, then its resource attributes include nax.feature.
refined: Given TracesInput with feature='my-feature' passed to buildTracesPayload, when the function returns a payload, then payload.resource.attributes['nax.feature'] === 'my-feature'.

original: When the OTLP module buildMetricsPayload creates a payload, then its resource attributes include nax.feature.
refined: Given MetricsInput with feature='my-feature' passed to buildMetricsPayload, when the function returns a payload, then payload.resource.attributes['nax.feature'] === 'my-feature'.

original: When buildHeartbeatMetricsPayload creates a payload, then its resource attributes include nax.run_id.
refined: Given HeartbeatMetricsInput with snapshot.attributes['nax.run_id']='run-123', when buildHeartbeatMetricsPayload is called, then the returned payload.resource.attributes['nax.run_id'] === 'run-123'.

original: When buildHeartbeatMetricsPayload creates gauge points, then their attributes still include the bare key feature.
refined: Given HeartbeatMetricsInput with snapshot.attributes['feature']='my-feature', when buildHeartbeatMetricsPayload is called, then for each gauge datapoint in the returned payload, datapoint.attributes['feature'] === 'my-feature'.

original: When the span-tree payload builder creates a payload, then its resource attributes include nax.project.
refined: Given span-tree builder called with project='my-project', when the builder returns a payload, then payload.resource.attributes['nax.project'] === 'my-project'.

original: When an incremental span flush is issued before run end, then its request resource attributes include nax.run_id.
refined: Given onRunStart has set runId='run-456' and a span is flushed incrementally via flushIncrementalSpan, when the flush returns a TracesPayload, then the payload.resource.attributes['nax.run_id'] === 'run-456'.

original: When git branch and sha resolution fails during onRunStart, then the hook completes without throwing.
refined: Given gitWithTimeout is stubbed to reject with an error, when onRunStart is called, then the call returns a resolved Promise and does not throw.

original: When git branch resolution fails during onRunStart, then a subsequent exported payload contains no nax.git.branch attribute.
refined: Given gitWithTimeout returns { sha: 'abc123', branch: undefined } (branch missing), when onRunStart completes and then buildTracesPayload or buildMetricsPayload is called, then the returned payload.resource.attributes does not contain 'nax.git.branch'.

original: When toLogRecord receives a known ISO-8601 timestamp, then timeUnixNano equals that instant in nanoseconds as a string.
refined: Calling toLogRecord({ timestamp: '2024-01-15T10:30:00.000Z' }) returns a LogRecord where timeUnixNano equals '1705315800000000000'.

original: When toLogRecord receives level error, then severityNumber is 17.
refined: Calling toLogRecord({ level: 'error', ... }) returns a LogRecord where severityNumber === 17.

original: When toLogRecord receives level error, then severityText is "ERROR".
refined: Calling toLogRecord({ level: 'error', ... }) returns a LogRecord where severityText === 'ERROR'.

original: When toLogRecord receives level warn, then severityNumber is 13.
refined: Calling toLogRecord({ level: 'warn', ... }) returns a LogRecord where severityNumber === 13.

original: When toLogRecord receives level info, then severityNumber is 9.
refined: Calling toLogRecord({ level: 'info', ... }) returns a LogRecord where severityNumber === 9.

original: When toLogRecord receives level debug, then severityNumber is 5.
refined: Calling toLogRecord({ level: 'debug', ... }) returns a LogRecord where severityNumber === 5.

original: When toLogRecord receives a message, then body.stringValue equals that message.
refined: Calling toLogRecord({ message: 'test message' }) returns a LogRecord where body.stringValue === 'test message'.

original: When toLogRecord receives a stage, then attributes contain nax.stage.
refined: Calling toLogRecord({ stage: 'implementation' }) returns a LogRecord where attributes contains a key 'nax.stage' with value 'implementation'.

original: When toLogRecord receives storyId, then attributes contain nax.story_id equal to it.
refined: Calling toLogRecord({ storyId: 'abc-123' }) returns a LogRecord where attributes['nax.story_id'] === 'abc-123'.

original: When toLogRecord receives no storyId, then attributes contain no nax.story_id key.
refined: Calling toLogRecord({}) returns a LogRecord where 'nax.story_id' is not a key in attributes.

original: When toLogRecord receives sessionRole, then attributes contain nax.session_role equal to it.
refined: Calling toLogRecord({ sessionRole: 'agent' }) returns a LogRecord where attributes['nax.session_role'] === 'agent'.

original: When data contains top-level string phase, then attributes contain nax.data.phase with that string.
refined: Calling toLogRecord({ data: { phase: 'testing' } }) returns a LogRecord where attributes['nax.data.phase'].stringValue === 'testing'.

original: When data contains top-level number count, then attributes contain numeric nax.data.count equal to it.
refined: Calling toLogRecord({ data: { count: 42 } }) returns a LogRecord where attributes['nax.data.count'].doubleValue === 42.

original: When data contains nested findings, then attributes contain nax.data_json with JSON containing that nested content.
refined: Calling toLogRecord({ data: { findings: [{ id: 1, severity: 'high' }] } }) returns a LogRecord where attributes['nax.data_json'].stringValue is valid JSON containing the nested findings array.

original: When data serialization exceeds 2048 characters, then nax.data_json is at most 2048 characters and ends with a truncation marker.
refined: Calling toLogRecord with data that serializes to more than 2048 characters returns a LogRecord where attributes['nax.data_json'].stringValue.length <= 2048 and endsWith('...').

original: When buildLogsPayload creates a payload, then its resource attributes include nax.feature.
refined: buildLogsPayload(resource, scope, record) returns an object where result.resource.attributes contains key "nax.feature" with a non-empty string value.

original: When OTEL reporter configuration omits logs.enabled, then it resolves to false.
refined: With config lacking a logs.enabled field, parseOTELReporterConfig(config).logs.enabled === false.

original: When OTEL reporter configuration omits logs.level, then it resolves to "info".
refined: With config lacking a logs.level field, parseOTELReporterConfig(config).logs.level === "info".

original: When logs.enabled is false and onRunStart runs, then addSink is not invoked.
refined: With logs: { enabled: false }, calling onRunStart() results in zero invocations of addSink.

original: When logs.enabled is true and onRunStart runs, then addSink is invoked exactly once.
refined: With logs: { enabled: true }, calling onRunStart() results in exactly one invocation of addSink.

original: When logs.level is "warn" and an info LogEntry is emitted, then no log record is posted.
refined: With logs: { enabled: true, level: "warn" }, emitting a LogEntry with severity "info" results in zero POST calls to the logs endpoint.

original: When logs.level is "warn" and a warn LogEntry is emitted, then a log record is posted.
refined: With logs: { enabled: true, level: "warn" }, emitting a LogEntry with severity "warn" results in exactly one POST call to the logs endpoint with a body containing a logRecord where severityText === "WARN".

original: When a LogEntry stage is "otel-batch-queue", then no log record is posted.
refined: With logs: { enabled: true }, emitting a LogEntry where entry.stage === "otel-batch-queue" results in zero POST calls to the logs endpoint.

original: When logs are enabled, message "no test command" is logged, and the queue flushes, then the posted body contains a log record whose body.stringValue equals "no test command".
refined: With logs: { enabled: true }, after emitting a LogEntry with body.message === "no test command" and calling flush on the logs queue, POST is called with URL ending in "/v1/logs" and the request body matches /\[\{"body":\{"stringValue":"no test command"/.

original: When logs are exported, then the request URL ends in /v1/logs.
refined: Every POST call made for log export has a URL pathname that ends with "/v1/logs".

original: When onRunEnd runs with queued log records, then it posts those records.
refined: Calling onRunEnd() when the logs queue contains N > 0 entries results in exactly one POST call with a body containing N log records.

original: When teardown runs after onRunEnd completed, then it posts no further logs request.
refined: After onRunEnd() completes (having posted), calling teardown() results in zero additional POST calls to the logs endpoint.

original: When a configured header references an unset environment variable and a log record is queued, then no logs request is posted.
refined: Given config.logs.headers contains a header value referencing an unset env var (e.g., "${UNSET_VAR}"), after emitting a log entry, POST is not called and the logs queue remains unflushed.

original: When a logs header references unset environment variables, then export is skipped and the reporter warns with the missing variable names without consuming a logs-queue retry.
refined: Given config.logs.headers references an unset env var, after emitting a log entry the warning log message contains the name of the missing variable and the logs queue retry count remains unchanged (not decremented).
